subject: Transitive Access Minimization & Vendor Proofs — Alder Health security request
messages:
From: Sasha Moore <security@alderhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request — transitive access minimization and key custody evidence

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the productive SIG call last week. Alder Health is running a focused gap assessment ahead of our procurement review and we have two asks that came out of the team:  

1) A minimal subprocessor roster for services that have persistent access to customer data or key material used in the inference runtime (we need the list scoped to production-only dependencies). CSV is fine.
2) Artifacts that demonstrate transitive-access minimization: i.e., how Redwood ensures downstream vendors cannot escalate access to customer keys or telemetry (preferably KMS delegation matrix, ephemeral credential TTLs, and any operator access process docs).

This is time sensitive for our procurement committee. Can you return the roster and a summary of the artifacts by EOD Wed (2026-08-26)? If an on-site evidence review is required for any provider, flag that and we can schedule.

Appreciate it,
Sasha Moore
Vendor Risk — Alder Health
security@alderhealth.com

Attachment: vendor-ask-20260824.pdf (stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Folks — forwarding Alder's ask. Sasha needs: (A) production-only subprocessor roster scoped to data/key access, (B) artifacts proving transitive-access minimization (KMS delegation, ephemeral key TTLs, operator access controls).

Plan I propose:
- Ben: can you pull the latest production subproc CSV scoped to inference runtime (exclude dev/test/devops-only vendors) and include hosting, kms, telemetry, and model-build partners?
- Jordan: can you assemble the KMS delegation matrix (who can create/delegate keys, escrow paths, region residency) and a short summary of ephemeral credential lifecycle (TTLs, rotation, short-lived impersonation flows)?

I will draft the covering email for Alder and package the attachments (csv + pdf + short one-page summary). If either of you thinks an on-site review will be requested for a provider, flag now — we should avoid surprises.

Target: compile artifacts by EOD Tue so we can respond Wed morning Alder time.

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request — transitive access minimization and key custody evidence

Naomi / Ben — attached the KMS delegation matrix and ephemeral key retention summary. Highlights for Alder:
- KMS delegation model: only the central Redwood KMS service account (kms-control@redwood) can create Root keys; delegated keys for compute (inference pools) are created with explicit audit entries and require an approval token from the key-ops queue. No downstream vendor can create long-lived keys usable for customer data without an escrow flow that Redwood controls.
- Ephemeral credentials: default TTL for inference worker tokens is 15 minutes; refresh requires signed session tokens and short-lived STS impersonation — documented in ephemeral-key-retention-summary.xlsx.
- Operator access: privileged operator sessions are tied to just-in-time approval with session recording; audit logs retained for 2 years for production incidents.

Attachment: kms-delegation-matrix.pdf (stub)
Attachment: ephemeral-key-retention-summary.xlsx (stub)

Jordan
Infra Security Engineer

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Moore <security@alderhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — transitive access minimization and key custody evidence

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear ask. Attached are the artifacts you requested scoped to production dependencies:  

1) redwood-subprocessor-roster-2026-08-25.csv — production-only roster; columns include vendor_name, service_role, residency, persistent_access_type, contractual_sla_ref.
2) kms-delegation-matrix.pdf — who may create/delegate keys, escrow/handback paths, and region residency notes.
3) ephemeral-key-retention-summary.xlsx — TTLs, rotation cadence, and short-lived session flow for inference workers.

Key clarifications:
- We do not permit downstream re-delegation of customer key material. Any vendor requiring access to plaintext or long-lived cryptographic material must be included in the roster and has a documented escrow path under Redwood KMS.
- Default inference worker tokens have a 15-minute TTL; privileged operator sessions use just-in-time approvals with session recording.
- For vendors that operate only test/development infrastructure we have excluded them from this CSV; contracts explicitly restrict escalation outside of Redwood-managed key flows.

If Alder would like to schedule an evidence review, we're available for a virtual walkthrough next week (I have Tue/Wed morning PT open). On-site reviews: none of the listed production vendors require a physical on‑site audit to validate the material above — we can provide additional audit logs or arrange vendor attestations if Alder's process requires it.

Links and artifacts:
- Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFgHIjKlMnOpQ
- Supplementary report (internal): https://redwood-docs.internal/reports/subproc-provenance-2026-08

Let me know if you want the attachments as a single signed bundle or need specific log slices for a date range.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-roster-2026-08-25.csv, kms-delegation-matrix.pdf, ephemeral-key-retention-summary.xlsx
